patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] nfsd: don't offer flexfiles layouts when NFSv3 isn't being served

version_history.subject: [PATCH] nfsd: don't offer flexfiles layouts when NFSv3 isn't being served

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch prevents the flexfiles layout driver from being offered when NFSv3 is not enabled, fixing a problem where clients would loop on NULL calls and hang in D state due to mismatched protocol versions.

review_comments.author: Chuck Lever
review_comments.summary: Applied the patch to nfsd-testing without issues and noted that it can be dropped if a better solution is found.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Fri, 04 Sep 2026 12:11:37 -0400, Jeff Layton wrote:
> The flexfiles layout driver hands out a deviceinfo that names this server
> as an NFSv3 DS (flexfilelayout.c hardcodes da->version = 3). With v3
> disabled, the client can't talk to the DS: it loops on v3 NULL calls that
> the server answers with PROG_MISMATCH, and I/O hangs in D state.
> 
> Skip LAYOUT_FLEX_FILES in nfsd4_setup_layout_type() unless v3 is enabled.
> 
> [...]

Applied to nfsd-testing, thanks! I can drop this one if you find a
better solution.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3] mm/memcontrol: skip non-hierarchical memcg-wide stats when v1 is unavailable

version_history.subject: [PATCH v3] mm/memcontrol: skip non-hierarchical memcg-wide stats when v1 is unavailable

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the Linux kernel's memory control group (memcg) statistics by skipping non-hierarchical memcg-wide stats when the v1 version is unavailable. This is done by compiling out the non-hierarchical arrays if CONFIG_MEMCG_V1 is not set, and skipping updates on these arrays even if v1 is supported but blocked by a boot parameter. The patch aims to reduce flush costs by avoiding unnecessary read-modify-write operations, resulting in a 4.1% reduction in memcg-wide aggregation time and a 2.2% reduction in overall flush function time.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 12/12] mm/collapse: implement MADV_COLLAPSE in madvise.c
patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch moves the implementation of MADV_COLLAPSE from khugepaged.c to madvise.c, where it belongs among other madvise operations. The move simplifies the code and removes unnecessary dependencies between the daemon's file and syscall code. The patch also includes a stub for !CONFIG_TRANSPARENT_HUGEPAGE configurations. The MADV_COLLAPSE operation remains a caller of the interface used by khugepaged, with no changes to its functionality.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 11/12] mm/collapse: declare the collapse interface in collapse.h

version_history.subject: [PATCH 11/12] mm/collapse: declare the collapse interface in collapse.h

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch declares the collapse interface in collapse.h, which includes functions and variables related to memory collapsing. The interface consists of four main calls: collapse_control_init, collapse_scan_pmd, collapse_run_pmd, and collapse_control_release. These functions are used for collapsing large pages and are currently static in khugepaged.c. The patch also renames hugepage_vma_revalidate to collapse_vma_revalidate as it is now part of the collapse interface. This change prepares the ground for implementing MADV_COLLAPSE in madvise.c, but does not introduce any functional changes.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 10/12] mm/collapse: work out the orders a VMA allows once per VMA

version_history.subject: [PATCH 10/12] mm/collapse: work out the orders a VMA allows once per VMA

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the calculation of allowed page orders in a VMA by computing it once per VMA instead of once per PTE table. This is done to reduce redundant work and improve performance. The patch also introduces a new parameter, `enabled_orders`, which is passed from the caller to the function that computes the allowed orders. This change allows for more efficient handling of hugepage-enabled knobs written during a walk.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 09/12] mm/collapse: open-code collapse_single_pmd() in its two callers

version_history.subject: [PATCH 09/12] mm/collapse: open-code collapse_single_pmd() in its two callers

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch removes the function collapse_single_pmd() and instead open-codes its logic in two callers, khugepaged's walk and madvise_collapse(). The original function had a complex locking contract that was simplified by giving up the lock before running the collapse. This change does not introduce any functional changes but simplifies the code.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 08/12] mm/collapse: separate scanning a PTE table from collapsing it

version_history.subject: [PATCH 08/12] mm/collapse: separate scanning a PTE table from collapsing it

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch separates the scanning of a PTE table from collapsing it into two distinct functions: collapse_scan_pmd() and collapse_run_pmd(). The scan function reads the PTE table under mmap_lock to determine if the range is worth collapsing, while the run function performs the actual collapse. This change improves code organization and allows for better tracing and reporting of collapse operations.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 05/12] mm/collapse: state what a collapse may do in the policy

version_history.subject: [PATCH 05/12] mm/collapse: state what a collapse may do in the policy

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new struct collapse_policy that allows the caller to specify what a collapse is allowed to do, such as setting limits on PTEs and determining whether to hold sub-PMD windows to stricter rules. The policy is filled in by khugepaged once per scan pass and by MADV_COLLAPSE once per call. This change simplifies the code by removing the need for tests scattered throughout the collapse path to determine what a collapse can do, instead allowing them to simply read from the policy struct.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 04/12] mm/collapse: add collapse.h for the collapse interface

version_history.subject: [PATCH 04/12] mm/collapse: add collapse.h for the collapse interface

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch adds a new header file, mm/collapse.h, to separate the interface and state of the collapse mechanism from its implementation in khugepaged.c. The new header defines an enum for scan results and a struct for control data, as well as two constants that were previously defined in khugepaged.c. This separation is intended to clarify the distinction between users and implementers of the collapse interface.

version_history.subject: [PATCH 00/12] mm/collapse: separate a collapse from its callers

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch set separates the collapse engine from its callers, introducing a clear interface and policy between them. The collapse engine is moved to khugepaged.c, but it now has an interface that allows callers to specify their own policies and interact with the engine without reaching into each other's code. The patch also moves MADV_COLLAPSE to madvise.c, where it belongs, and introduces four new calls: collapse_control_init, collapse_policy_set, collapse_scan_pmd, and collapse_run_pmd. This separation improves modularity and maintainability of the code.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the shared counter khugepaged_pages_collapsed being incremented by collapse_single_pmd(). They explained that the daemon should keep its own counter and not rely on the shared path to track who called, as it sees every result of every collapse. The author did not promise a fix in this reply.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the naming of the bitmap in khugepaged.c, explaining that it represents PTEs accepted as collapse sources and not just their presence. They agreed to rename it and update comments accordingly without any functional change.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged that the users of collapse and its machinery are intertwined in khugepaged.c, agreed to separate them by adding a new header file mm/collapse.h for shared definitions, and confirmed that no functional change is introduced.
review_comments.raw_body:
From: "Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta)" <kas@kernel.org>

khugepaged.c holds both the users of collapse and the machinery that
performs it.  The daemon's scan loop, the sysfs tunables, MADV_COLLAPSE's
entry point and the collapse itself all sit in one file and reach into
each other freely.  Nothing marks where a user ends and the engine
begins.

Start drawing that line.

Add mm/collapse.h for what the two sides have to agree on:

  - enum scan_result - what the engine hands back;
  - struct collapse_control - the state a request carries.

And two constants move with them:

  - KHUGEPAGED_MAX_PTES_LIMIT -> COLLAPSE_MAX_PTES_LIMIT;
  - KHUGEPAGED_MIN_MTHP_ORDER -> COLLAPSE_MIN_MTHP_ORDER.

Neither is a fact about the daemon, so both lose the KHUGEPAGED_ prefix.

No functional change.

Assisted-by: Claude-Code:claude-opus-5
Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
---
 MAINTAINERS     |  1 +
 mm/collapse.h   | 67 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 mm/khugepaged.c | 79 ++++++++-----------------------------------------
 3 files changed, 81 insertions(+), 66 deletions(-)

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the collapse_possible() function being unnecessary and only forwarding to collapse_possible_orders(). They acknowledge that its three callers can test the mask themselves, indicating no functional change.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern that tests scattered through the collapse path decide what a collapse is allowed to do by asking whether khugepaged started it, and explained that this should be handled by having the caller fill in a struct collapse_policy with their policy before calling the collapse code. The author confirmed that khugepaged fills the policy once per scan pass, MADV_COLLAPSE once per call, and made other minor changes to handle this new structure.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the naming of collapse_control_init_scan(), which was resetting values for each scan instead of once per control. The author agrees that the name points at the wrong thing and suggests renaming it to collapse_scan_reset() to reflect its actual purpose, with no functional change.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed concerns about the boundary between scanning and collapsing in collapse_single_pmd(), agreeing to split it into two separate functions: collapse_scan_pmd() for scanning, which reads under mmap_lock, and collapse_run_pmd() for collapsing, which wants the lock given up first. The author also explained changes to tracing and how scan results are communicated via the collapse_control structure.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed concerns about the locking contract in collapse_scan_pmd() and collapse_run_pmd(), agreeing to open-code the entry point in the two callers, khugepaged's walk and madvise_collapse(). Each scans under its own lock and drops it before running the collapse. The lock is given up and taken again at the same points as before, with no functional change.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 0/4] kernfs: three standalone fixes

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/4] selftests: cover kernfs file handles and same-parent rename
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds three tests to the kernfs selftest suite: decoding a file handle, decoding while the node is being removed, and looking up a name while an interface is renamed. Additionally, it includes two small fixes: counting only symlinks in ns_tag_isolates_class_net and skipping mkdtemp() failures instead of aborting.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/4] kernfs: take kernfs_rename_lock for same-parent renames too
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the kernfs_rename_ns function to take the kernfs_rename_lock lock even when renaming a node within its existing parent directory, not just when moving it to a new parent. This is done to prevent a bug where concurrent renames can create a path that never existed, and also to ensure that readers get a stable name. The patch takes into account the rare occurrence of renames and the fact that the lock is per filesystem, making it a reasonable trade-off for stability.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/4] kernfs: don't lose IN_DELETE_SELF when decoding a file handle
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the kernfs file system where IN_DELETE_SELF notifications are lost when decoding a file handle. The issue occurs because __kernfs_remove() clears i_nlink on a node's inode, making it invisible to subsequent passes that hash its inode. The patch takes a read lock on kernfs_rwsem to prevent this loss of notification and ensures that the inode is hashed before the ilookup() pass runs. This fix was tested with a 300ms delay between lookup and inode hashing, resulting in st_nlink being correctly set to 0 when removing a file in a cgroup directory.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 4/4] kernfs: fix up the unlocked attribute reads on the creation paths
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes two issues in the kernfs subsystem related to attribute reads during creation paths. In kernfs_create_link(), the code copies the target's owner attributes without holding a lock, which can lead to inconsistent ownership if the target is modified between the two reads. To fix this, the patch adds a lock to ensure both reads are done under the same lock. In kernfs_new_node(), the code reads the parent's mode and group ID for S_ISGID inheritance without holding a lock, but since the node does not exist yet, taking the lock would only introduce unnecessary contention. Instead, the patch marks these reads with READ_ONCE() to ensure consistency. The changes address issues introduced by a previous commit that allowed creating kernfs objects with arbitrary uid/gid.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses three independent issues in the kernfs subsystem of the Linux kernel. The first patch adds selftest coverage for decoding file handles and same-parent renames. The second patch fixes a bug where kernfs_rename_ns() takes the kernfs_rename_lock only when the parent changes, preventing potential path inconsistencies. The third patch resolves an issue where __kernfs_fh_to_dentry() creates inodes without locking, leading to inode hash collisions during rmdir operations. Finally, the fourth patch corrects a problem with kernfs_create_link(), which reads target uid and gid values unlocked, potentially resulting in incorrect ownership of created links.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 0/6] memcg: group struct fields by access pattern

version_history.subject: [PATCH 0/6] memcg: group struct fields by access pattern

series_items.subject: [PATCH 1/6] memcg: move per-node objcg to the read-mostly fields
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves the per-node object cgroup pointer from the end of a struct to the start, where it can be stored on a separate cache line from frequently updated fields. This is done to reduce contention and improve performance by minimizing the number of cache misses when accessing this field. The change has no functional impact.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/6] memcg: split mem_cgroup_private_id into two fields
series_items.patch_summary: This patch splits the `mem_cgroup_private_id` field in the Linux kernel's memory cgroup (memcg) code into two separate fields: `private_id` and `private_id_ref`. The original field had different access patterns for reading and writing, which is now addressed by separating these operations. This change allows a future patch to place these fields in different cache line groups, improving performance. No functional changes are made by this patch.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 3/6] memcg: group the write-hot fields of struct mem_cgroup
series_items.patch_summary: This patch groups the write-hot fields of struct mem_cgroup into a single cache line to improve performance by reducing cache line contention between read-mostly and write-hot fields. The fields are moved from their current scattered locations throughout the structure to a new group, which is aligned with a cacheline boundary. A new function, memcg_struct_check(), is added to ensure that any future changes to the struct do not move these fields out of their designated cache line group. This change has no functional impact on the system's behavior.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 4/6] memcg: group the cold fields of struct mem_cgroup
series_items.patch_summary: This patch groups the cold fields of struct mem_cgroup together to improve cache locality and reduce contention between hot and cold paths. The fields are moved from their current scattered locations in the struct to a single cache line group, which should improve performance by reducing false sharing. This change does not introduce any functional changes, only an optimization for better cache behavior.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 5/6] memcg: group the read-mostly fields of struct mem_cgroup
series_items.patch_summary: This patch groups the read-mostly fields of struct mem_cgroup together at the end of the structure, reducing false sharing between these fields and improving cache performance. The fields grouped include vmstats_percpu, vmstats, zswap_max, private_id, kmemcg_id, and oom_group. This change does not introduce any functional changes but optimizes memory access patterns. The grouping is done using a cacheline group boundary, which ensures that these fields are stored in the same cache line as nodeinfo[].

series_items.subject: [PATCH 6/6] memcg: group the fields of struct mem_cgroup_per_node
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the struct mem_cgroup_per_node to group its fields into named cache line groups, improving isolation and reducing padding. The changes are based on a previous commit that showed why lru_zone_size[] must not share a line with lruvec. The new grouping does not introduce any functional changes but may incur an extra cache line per node per memcg.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series aims to improve memcg performance by introducing a contract that ensures struct fields are sorted into named cache line groups based on access patterns, preventing false sharing and reducing the likelihood of performance regressions.
